text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **

German composer RICHARD WAGNER was born in 1813. He was best remembered for his series of "Ring" operas which centred around Norse mythology. His famous 'Ride of the Valkyries' was used as the soundtrack to the helicopter attack in the movie 'Apocalypse Now'.
British novelist SIR ARTHUR CONAN DOYLE was born in 1859. He was best remembered for creating 'Sherlock Holmes'.

LAURENCE OLIVIER was born in 1907. The British actor was the only member of his craft to be honoured with a peerage. LORD OLIVIER was associated with the theatre for many years, but is best remembered for his Shakespeare films. His performances of 'Richard the 3rd', and 'Hamlet' are considered the best ever.
Australian radio legend BOB DYER was born in America in 1909.

Australian rock star IVA DAVIES was born in 1955. As the frontman for 'The Flowers' he wrote and sang the Australian hits "Can't Help Myself", "We Can Get Together" and "Walls". A copyright dispute saw the band change its name to 'Icehouse' which was the name of the 'Flowers' first successful album. From 1983 they were internationally successful with hits such as "Hey Little Girl" (1983), "Crazy" (1987) and "Electric Blue" (1988).
** EVENTS **
337 : Constantine the Great, Roman Emperor, died. He was
largely responsible for turning the empire into a Christian state.
1455 : The first battle of the 30-year War of the Roses
was fought at St Albans between York and Lancaster. Lancaster won.
1840 : England officially stopped sending convicts to New
South Wales.
1860 : Queensland parliament met for the first time.
1885 : VICTOR HUGO, French poet, dramatist, novelist and
author of "Les Miserables", died.
1908 : WILBUR and ORVILLE WRIGHT patented their flying
machine. Their historic first powered flight had taken place in 1903.
1915 : The worst train disaster in Britain took place
when a troop train collided with a passenger train at Gretna Britain Green in Scotland, killing 227 people.
1921 : The City of Chicago said women with short skirts
and bare arms would pay fines from ten to one hundred dollars.
1938 : In Italy the Stromboli volcano erupted.
1959 : In the US the southern state of Alabama banned a
children's book for showing a black rabbit marrying a white rabbit.
1963 : In London Britain's first Communist peer sat in
the House of Lords. He was Lord MILFORD.
1975 : Rhodesia was expelled from the Olympics because of
its racial policies.
1981 : PETER SUTCLIFFE, the so-called Yorkshire Ripper,
was found guilty of murder of 13 women in Britain, and the attempted murder of seven others.
1982 : 5000 British troops landed in the Falkland
Islands. It was the first landing by the British in the Falklands' War.
1985 : 60 people were killed by a car bomb in Beirut.
1993 : Cambodia held its first multi-party election in 21
years. The elections followed a major peace proposal from Australia.
1994 : Sydney roadworker IVAN MILAT was arrested by
police during a dawn raid on his Eagle Vale home as a suspect in the backpacker murders. New South Wales police searched the house, south-west of Sydney and seized several items.
1994 : Rwandan rebels seized the key government army
barracks in Kigali, removing the biggest obstacle in their drive to capture the capital.
1996 : Japan settled lawsuits which bought to an end the
mercury poisoning case called Minamata, named after the village where hundreds died between 1953-60 by eating mercury-tainted seafood.
